request.deadline: 18-month funding period, with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Not-for-profit entity established or host-organization agreement signed, technical transition architecture and migration plan published, and public usage dashboard live in Q3 2026
Board election held via on-chain voting under published rules and newly elected board assumes mandate in Q4 2026
Public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod served by the new stack, Blockfrost IP legally transferred, and service performance maintained in Q1 2027
Public sustainability consultation, proposal publication, feedback process, and chosen direction documented in Q2-Q3 2027
Public API sustained at minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA during 2027 with quarterly technical and budget reports
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition under community-governed not-for-profit structure, with treasury administration involving Intersect and CDH as described
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed not-for-profit public API for Cardano and fund 18 months of transition and operations.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own node.
The proposal states that Blockfrost developer-survey usage grew from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025, citing Cardano Foundation survey links for each year.
The proposal states that Blockfrost served 781k unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data last month.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal states that more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the effort to decentralize Blockfrost operators.
The proposal commits to transferring Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.
The not-for-profit governance model would use a five-seat board with four seats for open-source infrastructure development entities and one community seat, preceded by a named preliminary board.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, calculated as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, for 18 months of transition and operations.
The budget allocates most funding to staffing for six roles, with additional allocations for infrastructure, DevOps-related operations, legal work, accounting, and entity or service migration costs.

The proposal says future sustainability may come from paid not-for-profit commercial tiers or a vendor-backed model, with profits or fees supporting the public API and potentially reducing future treasury reliance.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to move Blockfrost from a commercial/service-provider model into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with stated governance, IP-transfer, service-transition, reporting, and uptime deliverables across an 18-month period.
